Which State Has Produced the Most NBA Players? 🏀 Ever wondered which US states have sent the most players to the NBA? This video breaks down how many pro basketball players have come from different states across the country — a fun look at basketball talent by region, state by state. Here's the full breakdown: New York has produced 458 NBA players, one of the highest totals in the country. Big names include Michael Jordan, Donovan Mitchell, Carmelo Anthony, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Kentucky has sent 127 players to the NBA. Notable names include Rajon Rondo, Dave Cowens, Allan Houston, and Wes Unseld. California tops the entire list with 480 NBA players, the most of any state. Legends from California include Kawhi Leonard, LaMelo Ball, Russell Westbrook, and James Harden. Delaware has produced just 10 NBA players, one of the smallest totals. Names include Walt Hazzard, Donte DiVincenzo, Joey Graham, and Bones Hyland. Ohio is close behind New York with 222 NBA players. Notable names include CJ McCollum, LeBron James, Bronny James, and Steph Curry. Rhode Island has produced only 13 NBA players. Names include Joe Hassett, Tom Garrick, Marvin Barnes, and Ernie DiGregorio. Georgia has produced 162 NBA players. Big names include Dwight Howard, Jaylen Brown, Anthony Edwards, and Stephon Castle. Iowa has sent 31 players to the NBA. Names include Kirk Hinrich, Harrison Barnes, Keegan Murray, and Kris Murray. New Jersey has produced 168 NBA players. Notable names include Jalen Brunson, Dennis Rodman, Shaquille O'Neal, and Karl-Anthony Towns. Montana has produced just 11 NBA players, one of the lowest totals in the country. Names include Larry Krystkowiak, Phil Jackson, Coby Karl, and Adam Morrison. If you recognized any of these NBA legends, drop a Like!
